subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but adding this config surface changes public configuration, session-context behavior, and provider/auth routing semantics, which requires maintainer intent before automation should open another fix.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/context-pruning merge semantics to a later design item.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the open implementation PRs, leaving users to separate instances or global defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on the schema, agent-scope, and compaction helper paths where the public contract would land.
